questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Particular Solution of an Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs
questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ 0 & 2{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.

| ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ |  | $-10{e}^{-2t}$ |  | $\,,\,$ | ${x}_{p}(t)=\,\,$ |  | $2$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-1}} |  |  | {{field-2}} |  |  |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ 0 & 2{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{2t}\cdot 2{e}^{4t}-(-3{e}^{4t})\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{4t} & 3{e}^{4t} \\ 0 & {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-6t}}{2}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{4t} & 3{e}^{4t} \\ 0 & {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} & 3{e}^{-2t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-4t}\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{-2t} & 3{e}^{-2t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-4t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10{e}^{-2t} \\ -4{e}^{-4t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}-10{e}^{-2t} \\ -4{e}^{-4t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int -10{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -4{e}^{-4t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{-4t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -3{e}^{4t} \\ 0 & 2{e}^{4t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{-4t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -4 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -4\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -2{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & 2{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.

| ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ |  | $2{e}^{t}$ |  | $\,,\,$ | ${x}_{p}(t)=\,\,$ |  | $\frac{2}{3}$ |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-1}} |  |  | {{field-2}} |  |  |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -2{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & 2{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -4\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-t}\cdot 2{e}^{3t}-(-2{e}^{3t})\cdot 0}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{3t} & 2{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{2}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{3t} & 2{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t} \\ 0 & {e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}6 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 2{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -2{e}^{-3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ \frac{2}{3}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & -2{e}^{3t} \\ 0 & 2{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ \frac{2}{3}{e}^{-3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ \frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving an Inhomogeneous System of Linear ODEs Using Variation of Parameters
questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}5t \\ 7t\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form

| $x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}+\,\,\frac{1}{4}$ |  | $8t-14$ |  | . |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-1}} |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & 2{e}^{2t} \\ 2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}5t \\ 7t\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-t}\cdot {e}^{2t}-2{e}^{2t}\cdot 2{e}^{-t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -2{e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & -2{e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t} & 2{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}3t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int t{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=3t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=3\,\text{d}t$ and $v={e}^{t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3t{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t & =(3t)\cdot {e}^{t}-\int {e}^{t}\cdot (3\,\text{d}t) \\  & =3t{e}^{t}-3{e}^{t} \\  & =3{e}^{t}(t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=1\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int t{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t & =(t)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{2})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{2})\cdot (1\,\text{d}t) \\  & =-\frac{t{e}^{-2t}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{4} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{4}(2t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} & 2{e}^{2t} \\ 2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t}(t-1) \\ -\frac{{e}^{-2t}}{4}(2t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}12(t-1)-2(2t+1) \\ 24(t-1)-(2t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}8t-14 \\ 22t-25\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ 5 & 3\end{aligned}]x(t)+\overset{f(t)}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]}},\,Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & {e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{3t} & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of differential equations and the fundamental matrix of the corresponding homogeneous system above. Using the method of variation of parameters, compute ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)$ and the particular solution ${x}_{p}(t)$ of the system.

| ${Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)=\,\,$ |  | {{field-1}} |  | $\,,\,$ | ${x}_{p}(t)={e}^{t}\,\,$ |  | {{field-2}} |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | $2{e}^{3t}$ |  |  | $\frac{-19}{6}$ |  |  |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}0 & {e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{3t} & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{0\cdot (-{e}^{-2t})-{e}^{-2t}\cdot {e}^{3t}}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{-2t} \\ -{e}^{3t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =-{e}^{-t}[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{-2t} \\ -{e}^{3t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t} \\ {e}^{2t} & 0\end{aligned}] \\ {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-3t} & {e}^{-3t} \\ {e}^{2t} & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ 3{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-2t} \\ 2{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}5{e}^{-2t} \\ 2{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int 5{e}^{-2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int 2{e}^{3t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2}{e}^{-2t} \\ \frac{2}{3}{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & {e}^{-2t} \\ {e}^{3t} & -{e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{2}{e}^{-2t} \\ \frac{2}{3}{e}^{3t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}{e}^{t} \\ -\frac{19}{6}{e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={e}^{t}[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ -\frac{19}{6}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ -2 & -1\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the system of differential equations. Using the method of variation of parameters, the general solution of the equation can be written in the form

| $x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+\,\,$ |  | $-2t-3$ |  | . |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  | {{field-1}} |  |  |  |
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that the general solution of an inhomogeneous system can be written as 

$$
x(t)={x}_{c}(t)+{x}_{p}(t)
$$

where ${x}_{c}(t)$ is the complementary solution (solution of the corresponding homogeneous system) and ${x}_{p}(t)$ is a particular solution.

Notice that we are given that

$$
{x}_{c}(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-2t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}.
$$

We'll look for a particular solution in the form

$$
{x}_{p}(t)=Φ\,u(t)
$$

where $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix for the corresponding homogeneous system, $f(t)$ is the forcing column vector and

$$
u(t)=\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

In our case,

$$
Φ=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}4t \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Since $Φ$ is a fundamental matrix, it must be invertible. Using the formula for the inverse of a $2\times 2$ matrix, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{{e}^{-2t}\cdot {e}^{t}-(-{e}^{t})\cdot 2{e}^{-2t}}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} & {e}^{t} \\ -2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{-2t}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & {e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{Φ}^{-1}\,f(t) & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}{e}^{2t} & {e}^{2t} \\ -2{e}^{-t} & {e}^{-t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4t \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using our formula for $u(t),$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\int {Φ}^{-1}\,f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int [\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t} \\ -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\end{aligned}]\,\text{d}t \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\ \int -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Integrating the components by parts, we get the following:

- For the first component, let $u=\frac{4}{3}t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=\frac{4}{3}\,\text{d}t$ and $v=\frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{4}{3}t{e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{4}{3}t\cdot \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}-\int \frac{1}{2}{e}^{2t}\cdot (\frac{4}{3}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}t{e}^{2t}-\frac{2}{3}\int {e}^{2t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{2}{3}t{e}^{2t}-\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t}(2t-1).\end{aligned}
$$

- For the second component, let $u=-\frac{8}{3}t$ and $\text{d}v={e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t.$ Then, $\text{d}u=-\frac{8}{3}\,\text{d}t$ and $v=-{e}^{-t}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int -\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t & =-\frac{8}{3}t\cdot (-{e}^{-t})-\int -{e}^{-t}\cdot (-\frac{8}{3}\,\text{d}t) \\  & =\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}-\frac{8}{3}\int {e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{8}{3}t{e}^{-t}+\frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t}(t+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our particular solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{p}(t) & =Φ\,u(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-2t} & -{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{-2t} & {e}^{t}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3}{e}^{2t}(2t-1) \\ \frac{8}{3}{e}^{-t}(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}[\begin{aligned}(2t-1)-8(t+1) \\ 2(2t-1)+8(t+1)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2t-3 \\ 4t+2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
